summary: Round 2, verified by mutation in a private tree of the staged bytes (14 mutations, each run against RenameBlindnessTest + RedRecordWiringTest, tree restored and re-verified green after each). Both round-1 majors are CLOSED for test_integrity.py and for git_renames.py. M0.53-tr-1 (CI branch untested): killed -- pinning rename_map's args to ['--cached'] fails theCIModeFollowsRenamesToo AND NOTHING ELSE, as does reversing [base,'HEAD'] to ['HEAD',base]; that test is the sole killer of both. The production reviewer's major (id-preserving renames only): killed for test_integrity -- rekey returning `ident` unchanged, and rekey with from_pkg/to_pkg swapped, each fail exactly aPUREModuleMoveIsNotAnAccusationOfRemovingEveryTestInIt and aModuleMoveStillCatchesAWeakenedAssertionAsAWeakening. M0.53-tr-3 (vacuity survivor): killed -- narrowing tdd_scan's TEST_PATH to drop integrationTest now fails onlyAGENUINELYNewTestIsDemandedARecordNotTheOnesThatMerelyMoved, which the deleted absence-only test survived. M0.53-tr-2 (-M): killed -- `diff.renames false` in both fixtures makes dropping -M fail five of six tests. M0.53-tr-4 (R-guard): killed -- dropping startswith('R') fails theNameStatusParserFollowsRenamesButNotCopies and only that; swapping parts[1]/parts[2] fails five. M0.53-tr-1's tolerant copy loop is NOT a vacuity source: deleting scripts/git_renames.py fails all six RenameBlindness tests plus two RedRecordWiring tests, loudly. On the question about aPUREModuleMove's exit-0 assertion: it is not vacuous -- removing `paths = [q for q in paths if q not in sources]` from test_integrity.py fails that test AND NOTHING ELSE, and every mutation I could find that makes the gate examine nothing (MAIN_PATH never matching) is killed by three siblings. On the exact-equality in theNameStatusParser: appropriately tight, not over-tight -- the __main__ seam exists only for that test, so its format is not a contract with any other consumer, and equality is what kills the C-copy mutation that contains/doesNotContain would survive. All six red records verified against the STAGED blob: I recomputed tdd_scan.binding_key for each of the six ids over `git show :buildSrc/.../RenameBlindnessTest.java` and all six match .harness/tdd/red.json exactly. One MAJOR remains: the same rekey fix was applied to tdd_scan.py and is entirely unfalsified -- deleting the whole re-qualification block leaves the suite green, because the only fixture that reaches tdd_scan is the source-set move where from_pkg == to_pkg and rekey is a no-op. Suite total 6 in RenameBlindnessTest; no assertion in the existing RedRecordWiringTest was weakened (the only change adds git_renames.py to the copied-scripts list, and removing it fails two of its tests).

findings.title: tdd_scan.py's module-move re-qualification is completely unfalsified -- the whole rekey block deletes with the suite green
findings.failure_scenario: The class javadoc says the two shapes 'fail differently and round 1 conflated them', and the fix duly re-qualifies before-ids in BOTH scanners. But only test_integrity.py's half is tested against a module move. The two module-move tests (aPUREModuleMoveIsNotAnAccusationOfRemovingEveryTestInIt, aModuleMoveStillCatchesAWeakenedAssertionAsAWeakening) both invoke `bash scripts/check-test-integrity.sh` and never `python3 scripts/tdd_scan.py`. The only test that runs tdd_scan is onlyAGENUINELYNewTestIsDemandedARecordNotTheOnesThatMerelyMoved, and it uses the SOURCE-SET fixture, where before and after both declare `package binjava;` -- so from_pkg == to_pkg, rekey takes its first-line early return, and the entire re-qualification is a no-op on the only path any test exercises. This is the half that M4.2's own backlog row records as having cost real work: check-tdd treated 9 moved tests as NEW because every id changed from binjava.ingest.CommitLogTest# to binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#, and all 9 red records had to be re-earned against real mutations. I measured the regression directly: on a hand-built module-move fixture (ingest -> sequencer, package rewritten, `git config diff.renames false`, staged), the real tdd_scan.py prints `ok   no new tests in this diff` and exits 0; with the four-line rekey block deleted it prints `FAIL 2 new test(s) staged but no red record` naming binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#appliesDelta and #refusesEmptyCommit, and exits 1 -- a false accusation on a pure move, which is exactly the defect the block was written to fix. Nothing in the suite notices. This is the unfixed remainder of the production reviewer's round-1 major, not a new one: the fix landed in both scanners, but only one of them was made falsifiable. The closing assertion is small -- run `python3 scripts/tdd_scan.py check` against the EXISTING movedBetweenModules(dir, false) fixture and assert exit 0 with the four ids (both binjava.ingest.* and binjava.sequencer.* forms of CommitLogTest#appliesDelta and #refusesEmptyCommit) absent from stdout -- so this is a missing assertion rather than evidence the commit is too big.
findings.mutation_that_survives: In scripts/tdd_scan.py, delete the re-qualification entirely, leaving `was = test_ids(before, p)` / `fresh = test_ids(after, p) - was`: removes the `if origin != p:` guard and the `was = {rekey(i, package_of(before), package_of(after)) for i in was}` line. `./gradlew -p buildSrc test --tests binjava.RenameBlindnessTest --tests binjava.RedRecordWiringTest` exits 0, all tests pass. The `package_of(before)`/`package_of(after)` arguments swapped inside that same set comprehension survives for the same reason.

findings.title: rekey's `startswith(from_pkg + '.')` guard is unfalsifiable, and unlike java_tests.py's other defensive branch it is not recorded as such
findings.failure_scenario: Dropping the guard (`if from_pkg:` then slice unconditionally) leaves the whole harness suite green. It is not a test gap that can be closed honestly through the fixtures, because on every input the two call sites can produce, the guard's condition is already true: ids come from _scan, which qualifies them with PKG.search(normalise(src)), and from_pkg comes from package_of, which is PKG.search on the same source. The one construction that makes them disagree -- a block-commented `package binjava.old;` line at column 0 above the real declaration, visible to package_of on the RAW source and blanked by normalise before _scan sees it -- mangles the id under BOTH arms (with the guard: `binjava.sequencer.binjava.ingest.CommitLogTest#m`; without: `binjava.sequencer.st.CommitLogTest#m`), so no assertion could prefer one over the other. So the honest resolution is a comment, not a test. java_tests.py:182-189 already sets that precedent verbatim for the annotation-argument loop -- 'deleting it breaks no test, which is recorded rather than hidden' -- and this branch has no such note. A direct unit test of rekey over synthetic ids (the same seam-shaped move that git_renames.py's __main__ makes for parse_name_status) would be the alternative, and there is none: rekey is reached only through fixtures.
findings.mutation_that_survives: In scripts/java_tests.py rekey, replace `if from_pkg and ident.startswith(from_pkg + '.'):` with `if from_pkg:`. Suite green.

findings.title: tdd_scan's source-path filter is dead, but its comment claims parity with test_integrity's, where the same line IS load-bearing
findings.failure_scenario: Deleting `paths = [q for q in paths if q not in set(renamed.values())]` from tdd_scan.py leaves the suite green, and by inspection it can never matter: a rename's SOURCE does not exist at after_ref in either mode (':' with the path removed from the index, or 'HEAD:' in CHECK_RANGE mode), so `after = git('show', after_ref + p)` returns None and the loop's next line already takes `continue`. The comment above it -- 'See test_integrity: --name-only obeys diff.renames, the map does not' -- points at a line that is genuinely load-bearing there (removing test_integrity.py's identical filter fails aPUREModuleMoveIsNotAnAccusationOfRemovingEveryTestInIt and nothing else, because that scanner reads `before` for the source and reports every moved method a second time as a deletion). A reader who trusts the cross-reference will believe both lines carry the same weight and that both are covered; only one is. Either delete it, or record it the way java_tests.py:182-189 records its unreachable loop.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Delete the line `paths = [q for q in paths if q not in set(renamed.values())]` from scripts/tdd_scan.py check(). Suite green.

findings.title: A red record survives for the deleted round-1 test binjava.RenameBlindnessTest#aMovedTestIsNotMistakenForANEWOneNeedingAFreshRedRecord
findings.failure_scenario: The test was deleted as superseded by onlyAGENUINELYNewTestIsDemandedARecordNotTheOnesThatMerelyMoved, but its record remains. It is harmless today -- the gate demands records for ids present in the diff and never asserts the converse -- so nothing goes green that should not. It matters only as an accumulating fiction: red.json is the file a future reader consults to answer 'was this test ever observed failing', and it now names a test that does not exist. Not worth a gate; worth a line in the commit body or a sweep, and noted here rather than left for someone to trip over. The six live ids all bind correctly: I recomputed tdd_scan.binding_key over `git show :buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/RenameBlindnessTest.java` and every one matches its recorded sha256.
findings.mutation_that_survives: Not applicable -- this is harness bookkeeping, not a weakened assertion. Nothing in the staged diff is made to pass by it.
